user.title: Step 1 – Basics
user.description:
Welcome to **GridMetrics** – Tiered / Time-of-Use Electricity Rate Calculator.

Name your setup, choose how your utility bills you, pick your currency, and tell us if you have solar panels.

If you have solar (Enphase, SolarEdge, etc.) and a grid meter (Shelly 3EM, etc.), turn on **I have solar panels**. We will create Home Consumption, Grid Import/Export and Solar Production sensors for you automatically.

data.name: Name for this setup
data.rate_mode: How does your utility charge you?
data.currency: Currency shown on bills and sensors
data.billing_cycle_day: Day of the month your billing cycle starts (1–28)
data.fixed_charge: Monthly fixed / access charge (0 if none)
data.tax_percent: Tax / GCT / IVA percent (0 if none)
data.prepaid_enabled: I use a prepaid meter (buy credit in advance)
data.has_solar: I have solar panels (create net-metering sensors)

solar_production.title: Step 2 – Solar production
solar_production.description:
Select the sensor that shows how much power your solar panels are producing right now.

Prefer a **power** sensor in Watts (W). Enphase, SolarEdge and most inverters provide this.

Only tick the checkbox below if you only have a cumulative kWh energy sensor.

data.solar_is_energy: This sensor is cumulative energy (kWh), not live power (W)

grid_type.title: Step 3 – How is your grid measured?
grid_type.description:
Choose how your electricity meter reports power to Home Assistant.

• **Multiple phases** – you have separate sensors for phase A, B and/or C (typical with Shelly 3EM).
• **One single grid sensor** – one entity already shows net import/export for the whole house.

grid_phases.title: Step 4 – Phase sensors (Shelly 3EM style)
grid_phases.description:
Pick each phase power sensor you have. You can fill 1, 2 or all 3 – leave unused phases empty.

Example for Shelly 3EM:
• Phase A → sensor.shelly_3em_channel_a_power
• Phase B → sensor.shelly_3em_channel_b_power
• Phase C → sensor.shelly_3em_channel_c_power

The integration will add them together to get total grid power.

Then choose the sign convention (most meters: positive = importing from the grid).

data.grid_is_energy: These sensors are cumulative energy (kWh), not live power (W)
data.grid_sign: What does a positive number mean?
data.export_rate: Feed-in / export credit per kWh (0 if you get nothing for export)

grid_single.title: Step 4 – Single grid sensor
grid_single.description:
Select the one sensor that shows net power to/from the grid for your whole house.

Then choose the sign convention (most meters: positive = importing from the grid).

data.grid_is_energy: This sensor is cumulative energy (kWh), not live power (W)
data.grid_sign: What does a positive number mean?
data.export_rate: Feed-in / export credit per kWh (0 if you get nothing for export)

source.title: Energy source sensor
source.description: Select the cumulative energy sensor (kWh) that represents what you are billed for (total house consumption).

tiers.title: Consumption tiers (increasing block)
tiers.description:
Enter your utility’s block rates as: max_kWh:price, max_kWh:price, …

Aruba (Elmar) example:
500:0.3431,1000:0.3531,99999:0.4645

Mexico CFE-style example:
75:1.12,140:1.37,99999:4.00

Use a very high number (e.g. 99999) for the last tier.

tou.title: Time-of-Use periods
tou.description:
Enter periods as:
name|start|end|rate|weekdays_only
separated by semicolons.

Jamaica (JPS) example:
peak|18:00|22:00|0.35|true;partial|06:00|18:00|0.28|true;offpeak|22:00|06:00|0.22|false

weekdays_only = true means the period only applies Mon–Fri.
